title: Deployment-Driven Sales Activation Kit: Technical Storylines & Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook provides field sales, solutions engineering, and technical account teams with a single-page style toolkit for running deployment-driven pilots and accelerating expansion. It focuses on three levers buyers care about: measurable economics, predictable performance, and security controls. Use this doc during discovery, pilot design, and executive briefings.

Key outcomes this kit enables:
- Shorten pilot-to-contract cycle by reducing technical risk and clarifying success metrics.
- Equip sellers with crisp technical language and competitive differentiation for architecture and SLA conversations.
- Reduce legal/security cycles by surfacing standard answers and evidence.

Audience and when to use
- Sales Engineers: technical framing, demo checklists, POC success criteria.
- AEs and Solutions ETOs: value messaging for execs and procurement.
- Customer Security/Compliance: standardized FAQ and evidence links.
- Customer Success: onboarding checklist for day-1 production readiness.

Positioning and messaging summary

Core positioning statement
Redwood Inference is the inference platform that lets engineering teams move from experimental LLM proof-of-concept to predictable, cost-efficient production without rebuilding serving infrastructure. We combine a production-first runtime, policy-driven routing, and transparent economics so customers can control latency, cost, and availability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes.

Top three buyer messages (short)
1) Predictable economics: per-token and per-embedding transparency plus batching and cache controls that reduce unit costs by up to 5x vs ad-hoc self-hosted stacks.
2) Production reliability: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity with automated fallback to compatible model variants to meet 99.9% availability targets.
3) Enterprise controls: VPC/private deployments, KMS integration, and audit logging to meet regulated workloads.

Technical storylines for discovery calls
- Latency-first apps: highlight continuous batching, KV cache, and smart kernel selection to meet 50-200ms p95 token latency for short prompts on Dedicated tiers.
- Cost-constrained throughput: demonstrate batching/caching profiles and Optimize recommendations to model expected spend at target QPS.
- Data residency and isolation: present Redwood Private topology, KMS integration points, and audit log retention options.

Competitive brief (one-page table)
Competitor | Redwood advantage | Typical buyer objection | Short rebuttal
---|---|---|---
Large cloud AI endpoints | Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private | Buyer: cloud provider already has managed endpoints | Redwood: provides consistent SLA + predictable economics across regions and supports private air-gapped deployments that major providers do not offer out-of-the-box
Open-source self-hosting | Lower cost at scale but high ops burden | Buyer: we can run LLMs ourselves for cheaper | Redwood: reduces ops burden, provides quantization and kernel optimizations, and includes rollouts/fallbacks that reduce MTTD for regressions
Specialized inference vendors | Deep kernel tuning for specific hardware | Buyer: vendor claims better latency on niche hardware | Redwood: integrates kernel selection + routing and backs end-to-end SLOs with fallbacks and performance transparency for model variants

Pitch deck guidance and demo narrative (5 slides)
1) Problem slide: inconsistent latency, runaway inference costs, risky rollouts, and long ops cycles for custom stacks. Use customer stat: "66% of pilots stall due to serving complexity" (field sourced).
2) Value prop: show Redwood runtime, Optimize toolkit, and Console observability in a single diagram.
3) Demo: live generate (low-latency), show tracing and token-level cost KPI, then flip to dashboard showing canary rollout and regression alert.
4) Pricing & pilot: propose 8-week pilot, Dedicated trial credits, and success criteria.
5) Next steps & risks mitigations: security review path and escalation owner.

Pilot design template (numbered steps)
1) Align stakeholders: engineering, security, procurement, and a single executive sponsor.
2) Define success criteria: production QPS, p95 latency target, cost per 1M tokens, and qualitative tolerance for hallucination in top 100 prompts.
3) Select deployment mode: hosted API for feature proofs, Dedicated for latency/cost predictability, Private for regulatory needs.
4) Measure baseline: run standard prompt suite for 24 hours to capture token distribution, seq length, and cold/warm KV hit rates.
5) Configure runtime: batch policy, caching TTLs, quantization profile, and canary routing. Document config in 1 pager.
6) Run and iterate: weekly checkpoints, data for Optimize recommendations, and acceptance testing.
7) Hand-off: runbook and console dashboards delivered to customer success.

Technical configuration checklist (table)
Setting | Recommended default | Why it matters
---|---|---
Batch policy | 50ms dynamic batching / max batch 64 | Balances latency and throughput; reduces cost per token
KV cache TTL | 10 minutes for conversational workloads | Reduces repeated prefix compute; improves cold start behavior
Quantization profile | 8-bit dynamic for v2 models | Good latency/cost tradeoff; avoid for highest-fidelity ranking models
Tracing | Enabled with 7-day retention for pilot | Enables regression triage and cost attribution
SLO targets | p95 latency <= 250ms; availability >= 99.9% (Dedicated) | Standard commitments for production workloads

Pricing scenarios (short table)
Scenario | Suggested offer | How to sell it
---|---|---
Proof-of-value pilot | 8 weeks, Hosted credits 500k tokens, Free canary Dedicated hours (if applicable) | Frame as risk-free exploration with data to estimate run-rate
Deterministic production | Monthly Dedicated reservation with 6-month commit and burst capacity | Emphasize predictable unit economics and SLA
Private deployment | Annual platform license + onboarding fee + optional on-prem appliance | Position as compliance-first path with long-term TCO benefits

Short field scripts: objection handling
- Objection: "We already have model infra" 
  Rebuttal: "Great — Redwood complements existing infra. We can route non-sensitive requests through hosted API for fast time-to-value while keeping sensitive inference in Private to reduce ops overhead and accelerate product launches."
- Objection: "Your pricing is opaque"
  Rebuttal: "We will run a benchmarking pilot to produce a per-1M-token cost model using your real prompts. Console shows token-level breakdown during the pilot so nothing is hidden."

Reference case study (compact)
Customer: FinTech data enrichment platform
Challenge: Unpredictable latency during peak market hours and unclear inference costs across teams
Pilot approach: 6-week Dedicated pilot with sequence-length characterization, dynamic batching, and KV caching. We ran a synthetic 48-hour peak simulation to validate p95 and cost.
Results: Reduced 95th percentile token latency from 420ms to 180ms and achieved a 3x reduction in cost per generated token using quantization and batching recommendations. Pilot converted to an annual Dedicated contract.

Security & compliance FAQ (targeted for prospect security teams)
Q1: What deployment modes support customer-managed keys?
A1: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS on request. Hosted API supports per-customer encryption keys for stored artifacts.

Q2: How are logs/audit trails handled?
A2: Console provides audit logs for inference requests, model changes, and rollout events. Retention defaults to 90 days for pilots and is configurable up to 7 years for enterprise contracts. Logs can be shipped to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog) via secure forwarders.

Q3: Is data used for model training?
A3: We do not use customer inference data to train public models. For hosted API we provide an opt-out; for Dedicated and Private customer data remains under their control.

Q4: How do you handle vulnerability disclosures and patching?
A4: We maintain a public security disclosure policy and a quarterly patch cadence for managed components. Private customers can opt into an accelerated security patch SLA.

Q5: What certifications and audits are available?
A5: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is working toward ISO 27001. For enterprise Private deployments we provide evidence and can coordinate third-party audits under NDA.

Owners and next steps
